comment: Brian (ElevenLabs) VO for Episode 21 (300s): France vs Senegal, Group I, real kickoff Tue 16 Jun 2026 22:00. Canon: content/Stories/France-vs-Senegal.md (The Empire and the Lion). VERIFIED real facts: 31 May 2002, Seoul World Cup Stadium, the opening match of the 2002 World Cup - debutants Senegal beat reigning world champions France 1-0; Papa Bouba Diop scored after a scramble from El Hadji Diouf's cross and danced around his shirt by the corner flag (one of the iconic World Cup celebrations); Senegal then ran all the way to the quarter-finals; France crashed out in the group stage WITHOUT SCORING A SINGLE GOAL - the only defending champions ever to fail to score while defending the title. Papa Bouba Diop died on 29 Nov 2020, aged 42, of ALS (motor neurone disease). Senegal won their FIRST-EVER AFCON in 2022 (beat Egypt on penalties, Mane scored the winning kick after missing one earlier). RULES: Ep20 Iran-NZ recap labelled OUR PREDICTION (we predicted 1-1). This ending is OUR PREDICTION (France 2-1 Senegal). Soccer only - round-neck shirts, a pitch with goals, NO helmets/pads/gridiron. Honour Bouba Diop respectfully. Lines short - never tempo-stretch.

lines.text: In two thousand and two, the World Cup opened — and the smallest team on the pitch knocked out the champions of the world.
Tonight, those same two nations meet again. And in the stands, a man is dancing — for someone who is gone.
Last time, we predicted Iran and New Zealand would draw one-all. Tonight: the empire... against the lion.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends, episode twenty-one. France versus Senegal — the colonizer, and the colonized, on the same green grass.
And stay with me — because the story of this fixture is one of the greatest shocks football has ever seen.
First, the history. And this one is true. Seoul, the thirty-first of May, two thousand and two. The opening match of the whole tournament.
France were the reigning world champions — Zidane, Henry, Vieira. Senegal had never played a World Cup game in their lives.
Half an hour in, a cross fizzes across the six-yard box, the defence panics — and a giant midfielder pokes it home.
Papa Bouba Diop. He pulled off his shirt, laid it on the corner flag, and the whole team danced around it. Senegal one, France nil.
It did not stop there. Senegal ran all the way to the quarter-finals. France went home without scoring a single goal — the only champions ever to fail like that.
Papa Bouba Diop left us in twenty-twenty, far too young. But that dance never died. Tonight, it walks out again.
France. Les Bleus. World champions, finalists, the deepest squad on the planet — and at the front of it, a phenomenon.
Kylian Mbappe. Captain. The fastest forward in the game — thirty-eight kilometres an hour, and a finish as cold as ice.
Beside him, Ousmane Dembele and Michael Olise — two of the most dangerous wingers in Europe, in red, white and blue.
And behind them, Aurelien Tchouameni shields the back, with William Saliba — a wall barely old enough to be its captain.
Champions, head to toe. But across the line stands a nation that has beaten France before — and remembers exactly how.
Senegal. The Lions of Teranga. In twenty-twenty-two they won their first-ever Africa Cup of Nations — and the man who scored the winning kick is still here.
Sadio Mane. From a tiny village in Casamance to the top of the world — Champions League, Premier League, his country's greatest-ever forward.
Behind him, Kalidou Koulibaly marshals the defence, Lamine Camara drives the midfield, and Edouard Mendy stands tall in goal.
With Nicolas Jackson up top, this is no underdog story anymore. These Lions believe.
So here is the duel. France's golden machine against the heirs of two thousand and two. The empire... against the lion.
Our prediction — built on French firepower, on Senegalese pride, and on a fixture that has stunned the world once already. Watch.
France strike first. Dembele slips it inside, Mbappe is gone before the defence can blink — one-nil, Les Bleus.
But the Lions answer. Mane drifts left, the cross hangs, and Nicolas Jackson rises to head it home. One-all.
Then, late, the champions find one more. A loose ball, a flash of blue — Mbappe again. Two-one, France.
France two, Senegal one, in our story — the empire holds on, the lion roars to the very end. Both sides leave everything on the grass.
Do you agree? Comment LES BLEUS if France are simply too strong. Comment LIONS if Senegal shock the world all over again.
And the man dancing in the stands? Legend number twenty-one: the Dancing Lion. He keeps a folded shirt and a corner flag close to his heart.
He dances for Papa Bouba Diop, and for the night a continent believed. Find him inside the game.
